summary:
The post effects of GDD 16.4 are built and committed on m10/postfx (726c2f9), and tools/check.sh prints CHECK OK on that commit. One thing differed from the brief: the worktree was at 524fdab (docs only), not 88a7899, so I created m10/postfx from 88a7899 in it; the worktree's own branch is untouched.

A CanvasLayer "PostFX" in scenes/drive.tscn (between Sky and Overlay, so under the pointer and the HUD) carries src/view/post_fx_view.gd (PostFxView), which runs shaders/post_fx.gdshader on a full-screen rectangle. The drive controller calls setup(data, camera, cabin) once and apply(snapshot, delta) each frame: three lines there, one ext_resource and one node in the scene. The shader takes the nine named uniforms: tunnel, lids, blink, haze, rain_blur, cracks, glare_amount, glare_position, darkness. All 47 strengths, colours and sizes are in a new group post_fx_view in data/tuning.json, each with a unit.

How haze keeps the cabin readable: a canvas shader cannot read depth, so the glass is found by geometry. Each pixel's ray is taken into the cabin frame and met with three panes (windscreen, two side windows) given in tuning; whatever is drawn under the Cabin's Mirror and Visor nodes is taken out again. Haze, rain blur and cracks are on the windscreen only, and the lowest 5 cm of glass above the dash stay clear, so the clock and what stands on the dash stay sharp. Night and glare apply in full outside every window and only as a share on the cabin. Tunnel, lids and blink lie over everything.

The blur is a real one: the Compatibility renderer does generate mipmaps of the screen texture for a canvas shader, so no approximation was needed. Every amount is eased and may not reverse within 0.17 s of its last reversal, which caps any effect at three flashes a second whatever the snapshot does. With nothing to show, the rectangle is hidden and the screen is not copied.
verification:
All rendering was under xvfb with gl_compatibility / opengl3 (llvmpipe); no run printed an ERROR or SHADER line.

- **tools/check.sh** on commit 726c2f9: CHECK OK (parse 81 scripts, data 332 tuning constants, tests RESULT: OK with 88 of 114 passing as before, smoke 2 scenes and 5 runs with 0 failures, so the drive scene with PostFX runs headless on night, roadworks, motorcade, rain and a Telling).
- **Renderer probe** (throwaway script): a canvas_item shader on a CanvasLayer reads the 3D view through hint_screen_texture; textureLod at levels 0, 2, 4 and 6 gives progressively smoother bands, so mipmaps exist; SCREEN_UV starts at the top left; a later CanvasLayer stays sharp on top. The docs_api dump holds signatures only and says nothing on this.
- **tools/post_fx_check.gd** (headless): 128 checks, 0 failures. It checks that the shader declares the nine uniforms, that the view sets every uniform the shader declares, that each of the nine follows its snapshot key and returns to 0, the light's place, and two legs of the real DriveSim (Night behind sunglasses gives darkness 0.83; Rain unwiped for 7 s gives rain_blur 1.0). Throwing each key back and forth every 1 to 21 frames for 10 s never produced more than 6 reversals in any second.
- **Mutations of that check**: postfx_flash_hold set to 0 gave 10 failures (60 reversals a second); removing one uniform write and breaking the darkness formula gave 3 failures. Both were restored.
- **Legs from the drive scene, pictures read**:
  - `--leg=night,2 --bot=line --hud`, frame 300: headlight pool, dark sides, dim cabin, HUD crisp on top (artifacts/m10_postfx_darkness.png).
  - `--leg=rain,1`, frame 180: HUD reads blur 0.50, half blurred. Frame 480: HUD reads 1.00, vehicles are smudges, cabin and clock sharp, streaks on every window (m10_postfx_rain_blur.png).
  - `--leg=motorcade,3`, frame 2400: HUD reads Glare 80 and Nerves 98; wash and blaze straight ahead, plus the Tunnel's dark edges driven by the same simulation (m10_postfx_glare.png).
- **tools/post_fx_shots.gd, pictures read**: tunnel at 1.0 and 0.5, lids at 0.25, a blink caught mid-way, eyes shut (mean brightness 0.019), haze at 0.6, haze with the eyes turned to the glovebox, haze in a dust haze, rain wiped and full, cracks at 0.2 (and with the eyes on the gear lever, the web stays on the glass), glare as spotlight and as sun, night at low beam, high beam, dead headlight and behind tint, eyes left and right, and everything at once. Nine of these are in artifacts/ as m10_postfx_<state>.png.
- **Glass mask**: stays on the glass under a glance and in a 1280x960 window; the mirror stays crisp under haze, and so does the lowered visor (a throwaway probe showed its node by hand: its pixels stayed #1c1c20 while the glass below was hazed).

Not run: Forward+ and Mobile (no Vulkan on this machine).
decisions: The files are shaders/post_fx.gdshader and src/view/post_fx_view.gd (PostFxView, on the CanvasLayer PostFX in drive.tscn between Sky and Overlay) rather than the postfx.gdshader and postfx.gd of GDD 13.2; the layer keeps the default layer number and lies under the pointer and the HUD by its place in the tree.
PostFxView.setup(data, camera, cabin) takes the camera and the Cabin node, and apply(snapshot, delta) takes the frame's delta as RoadView does, so easing runs in real frame time.

Because a canvas shader cannot read depth, the glass is found by geometry: each pixel's ray is met in the cabin frame with three panes given in tuning (postfx_windscreen, postfx_window_left, postfx_window_right), and up to four things drawn under the Cabin's Mirror and Visor nodes are taken out again.

Haze, rain blur and cracks are on the windscreen only, while the night, the glare and the falling rain are outside every window; the cabin takes 40% of the darkness (postfx_cabin_darkness_share) and 15% of the glare (postfx_glare_cabin_share).

The lowest 5 cm of windscreen above the dash stay clear and the windscreen's effects reach full strength at 10 cm (postfx_demist_strip), so the clock and what stands on the dash stay readable and the nearest 12 m of road stay sharp, while everything beyond about 22 m is fully affected.

Haze is a veil never thicker than the snapshot's haze, thinning in slowly drifting patches; it is smoke-coloured, and takes sky_color_dust whenever the view ends by day, because the snapshot does not say what the haze is made of.
Rain blur is taken from the screen texture's mipmaps with five taps, up to 2% of the view's height at rain_blur 1 (postfx_rain_blur_radius), and streaks fall outside every window while it rains.

'Cracks cover 20% of the view' is read as that share of the windscreen's glass: a web in a disc of that area around a point of impact at the middle of the windscreen, fixed to the glass, whose shards shift what is seen through them.
Glare is a wash of the snapshot's strength at the light, fading with distance, with a small blaze at the light itself; the cabin gets 15% of it.

glare_position is worked out each frame from a direction from the car: the snapshot's glare_position if it has one (Vector2, degrees right and up), else the sun's side when sun is above 0 (sun_side times postfx_sun_position), else postfx_glare_position (straight ahead, the spotlight).

At night what the headlights do not reach loses 80% of its light (postfx_night_darkness), and night_darker takes its share of what is left both there and inside the pool, so sunglasses and tinted glass darken the lit road too.
The headlights' pool is an ellipse around straight ahead whose size is visibility divided by low_beam_cone, so high beam, a dead headlight, fog lamps and sunglasses all show.

For Tunnel, what is left of the view is an ellipse shrinking from the whole view at tunnel_from to tunnel_min_view at Nerves 100, and the dark edges come up to strength over the first 15% of that way (postfx_tunnel_onset) so the tell appears without a jump.
Lids are soft-edged bars that reach a little further at the sides and cover the snapshot's share in the middle; a Blink or Nod sweeps them shut and open again in 0.06 s (postfx_blink_time).

The three-flashes rule is enforced in the view: every amount is eased (postfx_fade_time) and one that has reversed may not reverse again for 0.17 s (postfx_flash_hold); falling rain moves but leaves the picture's overall brightness steady.
With nothing to show, the full-screen rectangle is hidden, so the renderer neither copies the screen nor runs the shader.
The load_steps count in drive.tscn's header was left as it was: Godot 4.7.2 no longer writes it when saving a scene, and leaving the line alone keeps the scene edit to one ext_resource and one node.

Two tools were added, tools/post_fx_shots.gd (pictures of states set by hand over the drive scene) and tools/post_fx_check.gd (headless check of the wiring and the flash rule); neither is a registered test nor a step of check.sh.
The twelve new pictures in artifacts/ were re-compressed losslessly (same pixels) to keep the folder small.
left_undone: Forward+ and Mobile were not run (no Vulkan here); only gl_compatibility was rendered.
tools/post_fx_check.gd is not in the gate: tests/tests.json was off limits and I left tools/check.sh alone; one line there (run_step postfx --script res://tools/post_fx_check.gd) would add it.
docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/PROGRESS.md still need their entries for this piece.

A hand raised to the visor or the mirror, and what hangs on the mirror where it sticks out past it, are clouded, blurred and darkened with the glass; only what is drawn under the Cabin's Mirror and Visor nodes is told apart.
The side windows are never clouded or blurred; they are only darkened, dazzled and rained on.
The placeholder cabin has a 13 cm gap between each door and the floor; at night the lit ground shows through it as a bright band when he looks far down to a side, because that gap is not glass.
Frame time was not measured on a GPU (llvmpipe only); while any effect shows, the screen is copied with mipmaps every frame.
The Wreck's cut to black and the prologue's white-out are not among the nine uniforms and were not built.
postfx_sun_position (60 degrees at sun_side 1, 7 degrees up) is my guess and must be matched to where the sky draws the sun once the boss views exist.
needs_from_simulation: glare_position: where the light behind the Glare is, as a Vector2 of degrees right of straight ahead and degrees above the horizon. Without it the motorcade's spotlight is drawn straight ahead whichever lane its car is in and however the road bends, and the sun's height is a view constant.

sun and sun_side: not in commit 88a7899. I saw them in the main checkout's working copy (read only: sun is the low sun's strength before the visor, sun_side runs from -1 far left to 1 far right) and the view reads them when the snapshot has them. That path is tested only with hand-made snapshots, so please confirm the meaning holds at merge.
What the haze is made of, for example a haze_dust share: today the veil is dust-coloured whenever visibility is finite by day and smoke-coloured otherwise.

summary:
The sound of GDD 16.5 is built and committed on local branch m10/audio (c650004, not pushed); tools/check.sh prints CHECK OK on it. I could not listen to anything here: the sounds were checked by measurement, spectrograms and an offline recording of the real mix.

Two things to know before merging:
- The worktree was at 524fdab (main), not 88a7899 as the task said, so I created m10/audio from 88a7899 inside the worktree and worked there.
- data/sfx.json is rewritten in a new vocabulary. Any sound another branch adds in the old shape (wave "click", "notes", "thump" and so on, no rate, peak or gain_db) is an error at boot and must be rewritten at merge.

How it works:
- **Generator** (new src/game/sfx_synth.gd): turns one "synth" entry into a 16-bit mono AudioStreamWAV. An entry names a wave (sine, saw, square, noise), a pitch (freq with optional glide or trill, several freqs together, or a row of notes and rests), an optional filter that may sweep, and envelopes (attack, release, decay, per-note shapes, bursts). Loops are made seamless. A key that nothing reads, or that means nothing for that sound, is an error at boot.
- **Data** (data/sfx.json): 32 entries, the 31 of the table plus `engine_harmonic`. The same entry also says how the sound is played: gain_db, loop, fades, hold, functional and duck_*, every, per_minute, speed_kmh, speed_hz, idle_hz, per_gear, warble. A "stream" file replaces the generated buffer.
- **Audio autoload** (src/game/audio.gd): one player per sound.
  - Events: plays every `sfx_requested`; a `hit` (scrape, or crash for crash and head-on); a `close_call` (squeal_1 to squeal_8 by "chain"); `heckle_started` (the ding).
  - `Audio.apply(snapshot)`, one line added to drive_controller.gd, drives the engine, rumble strip, heartbeat, radio or tape, siren, phone, indicator tick, Phantom hum and the horn of a Snap. It steps by the snapshot's "time" and goes quiet when snapshots stop.
- **Mix**: the four functional cues play on a "Cues" bus, everything else on "Bed"; while a cue sounds, Bed is turned down by that cue's duck_db.
- **Tool**: tools/audio_check.gd (with tools/audio_drive_check.gd for the parts that need the autoloads) measures every buffer, checks the entries against the table, weighs the mix, and steps Audio through drive states. I also added it as a step of tools/check.sh (two added lines); drop them if you would rather not have it there.

One bug worth naming: Godot reads past a loop's end as it turns. Without the loop's first 8 samples repeated after its end, the car-engine loop and the hum clicked on every turn; this showed only in the offline recording and is fixed.

Does the check have teeth: I planted 63 faults one at a time in audio.gd, sfx_synth.gd and sfx.json (wrong pitch law, squeal off by one, no ducking, siren while pulled over, loop tail missing, shared stream file mutated, and so on). All 63 were caught. The first such run exposed that the tool was dropping the drive-state failures; that is fixed, and two real flaws it then showed were fixed too.

Offline recording of the real mix: a 72 s scripted tour of every sound through the Audio autoload, recorded with --write-movie under xvfb with --audio-driver Dummy, then analysed with numpy and read as spectrograms.
- Engine: 120 Hz saw at 100 km/h with the gear-3 harmonic at 480 Hz; on shifting to 4th and 2nd the harmonic jumps to 3x and 5x and the pitch follows speed; idles at 30 Hz.
- Ducking, measured on the engine's 120 Hz line: -24.0 dB falls to -37.0 dB during a yawn (exactly the 13 dB of duck_db) and is back within 0.3 s; about -39 dB on the rumble strip; -37.4 dB at each indicator tick, recovering to -34.3 dB between ticks.
- Squeals rise over nine close calls with the last two equal; heartbeat interval shortens from 1.0 s to about 0.55 s as Nerves go 80 to 100; siren gaps shorten 3.0 s, 2.25 s, 1.5 s; horn held 2 s through a Snap.
- No clicks at loop turns after the loop-tail fix; the recording before it had a spike every 50 ms on the engine.

Real legs headless with I99_AUDIO_LOG=1 on the committed code:
- night,3 with a phone: rings at frames 2089, 2172, 2256, 2340 (four rings in the 5 s call, the simulation's own first ring not doubled); hum from 2700 to 2799.
- patrol,2: 14 siren chirps, the first when the lights appear.
- rain,1 with a mixtape: radio_music plays instead of static.
- No error lines and no leak warning at exit in any of them.

The task's own example command (xvfb, opengl3, --audio-driver Dummy, --leg=night,2 --bot=line --hud --shot) ran without errors and the picture is unchanged.

A WAV imported into the project and named as "stream" was tried three ways (the importer's own loop, compressed without a loop, uncompressed without a loop). The uncompressed loop turned without a click; the compressed ones tick faintly, as the engine's own imported loops do.
decisions: Every sound is described by its sfx.json entry in a small vocabulary (wave sine/saw/square/noise; pitch as freq with freq_to or trill, freqs, or notes with rests; partials or harmonics; filter with cutoff, cutoff_to, q; attack, release, decay, note_*, burst_hz, burst_decay; rate, duration, peak, seed), and the same entry carries how it is played; a key nothing reads, or one that means nothing for that sound, is an error at boot.

Buffers are 16-bit mono at 22050 Hz (11025 Hz for the radio loops, the yawns and the hum), all normalised to peak 0.9, with loudness set by gain_db at playback; making all 32 at boot takes about 70 ms.
The engine is one saw loop at 60 Hz whose player pitch follows speed on the line through 40 km/h = 60 Hz and 160 km/h = 180 Hz, unclamped above and held at idle_hz 30 Hz below; a Wreck fades it out.

The per-gear harmonic is a second entry, engine_harmonic (a sine loop), tuned to harmonic 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 of the engine's pitch in gears 1 to 5 and silent in neutral, so shifting up drops the added note as revs would.
The heartbeat is heard only during Pound (its tell in GDD 5.8), at 60 a minute where Pound begins (pound_from) rising linearly to 120 a minute at snap_at.

Functional cues play on their own bus and, while one sounds, everything else is turned down by that cue's duck_db; the depths (yawns 13 dB, rumble strip 15 dB, indicator 13.5 dB) are set so each cue stands at least 6 dB above every other sound at once at its loudest, which is the tool's reading of 'audible over everything else'.

The indicator ticks again every 0.4 s for as long as the indicator signals, so the player hears it is still on; its duck releases over 1.2 s so the rest stays down between ticks rather than pumping; the hazard lights tick only when toggled.

The siren gives one chirp when the blue lights appear and then chirps every 3.0 s at no Suspicion down to every 0.8 s at full Suspicion while police_lights or suspicion_watching is true, and is silent while pulled over.

The phone rings again every 1.4 s while snapshot caller is set (four whole rings in a 5 s call) and is cut the moment the call ends; the simulation's own sfx_requested for the first ring is not doubled.
The horn is a loop that sounds for hold 0.4 s per request and for as long as snapshot snap lasts.
The Phantom's hum is a 55 Hz sine with two weak harmonics (110 and 165 Hz) so small speakers carry it; it sounds while cramp is "hum", or for hold 1.5 s if only requested.
The radio plays the loop of its station, or static; a tape in the deck plays radio_music whatever the dial says, and past the end of its side the pitch wavers by 5% at 3 Hz.
A close call plays squeal_(chain+1), capped at squeal_8; a scrape hit plays scrape, a crash or head-on plays crash; heckle_started plays the ding; the rumble strip sounds only while the car moves.
The sound steps by the snapshot's own "time" (at most 0.25 s per frame), so repeats keep simulation time, and snapshot-driven sounds fall silent when no snapshot has come for two frames.
There is no limiter: Godot's AudioEffectHardLimiter was measured to leave its bus up to about 1.5 dB quieter after it has limited, so a rare pile-up may clip briefly instead.
Every loop buffer is followed by its own first 8 samples because Godot's resampler reads past loop_end; a filtered loop has its filter run in round the loop first.
A "stream" file is never modified: an entry that must loop it, or must not, plays a copy; plain PCM loops get the same 8-sample tail, compressed ones loop as the importer would.
At exit Audio stops every player and waits two mixer steps, so the engine does not report the playing sounds as leaked objects.
tools/check.sh gains a step, audio, that runs tools/audio_check.gd after the data validator.
Setting the environment variable I99_AUDIO_LOG prints every sound that starts or ends, for tracing real runs without touching the argument list in game.gd.
left_undone: docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/PROGRESS.md are not updated (by instruction); the decisions above need recording.

Nothing was heard by ear: levels and character were judged from measurements, spectrograms and the offline recording, so the gains and duck depths in sfx.json are a first pass for someone with speakers.

The duck depths are strong in ordinary play (the engine and radio drop 13 to 15 dB during a cue, and stay about 10 dB down for the up-to-5 s the indicator signals); they follow from the 6 dB worst-case rule and can be eased in sfx.json if that rule is relaxed.
Looped files supplied as "stream" should be imported uncompressed (or as Ogg): Godot's default QOA compression makes a loop tick faintly as it turns, the same as the engine's own imported loops.
No volume or mute setting (GDD 17.1 lists none) and no HUD row for sound (debug_hud.gd and the line files are shared).
All sounds are mono and centred.
Under --write-movie only, the engine still reports two leaked objects at exit (the mixer does not run during the exit wait in that mode).
No recordings or spectrograms are in the repository (artifacts/ was not among the folders I could add to); `tools/audio_check.gd -- --wav=<folder>` writes every buffer as a .wav for listening.
needs_from_simulation: A snapshot key for the tape deck (for example "deck": "", "playing" or "warbling"): today a playing tape is inferred from effects containing "music" while radio is "static", and a warbling one from an item's "warbling".
Dawn's call on his own phone (M7) should set snapshot "caller" while it rings, or emit phone_ring for each ring; with only one sfx_requested it will ring once.
If Suspicion at the Checkpoint should not chirp like a patrol car, the snapshot needs to say who is watching; today any suspicion_watching or police_lights chirps.
Snapshot "time" must stay the simulation's running clock in seconds: Audio steps by it.
Events or snapshot state for the wedding guests' clap and ululation, and heckle_started, when the frame is built (M9).

summary:
Subtitles are built and committed on the local branch m10/subtitles (one commit on top of 88a7899, not pushed), and tools/check.sh prints CHECK OK on that commit. One thing differed from the brief: the worktree was at 524fdab (docs only), not 88a7899, so I created the branch with `git checkout -b m10/subtitles 88a7899`; the harness branch worktree-wf_9e18e3ba-75d-3 still points at 524fdab.

How it works: a CanvasLayer "Subtitles" in scenes/drive.tscn runs src/view/subtitles_view.gd (SubtitlesView). It listens to `line_requested` on the Events bus (payload "id"), looks the line up through Lines and shows it at the bottom centre: the speaker's name in a row of its own over at most two lines of 42 characters, held for max(1.5 s, 0.06 s per character). The wrapping, timing and queue are the pure class SubtitleQueue (src/view/subtitle_queue.gd, RefCounted, no Node): text is cut at spaces, two lines are balanced, a longer text is shown in two-line parts each timed by its own length, and lines arriving meanwhile wait in order. A row that holds an exchange ("Guest, then Abu Noor" / "a / b") is shown as one subtitle per speaker. Speaker names are lines of their own (`speaker.old_woman` etc., via the new Lines.get_speaker_name); nine were added to both CSV files, with empty text and needs_writer true in lines_ar.csv. Both labels have automatic text direction. `clear()` empties it; the view calls it on a `wreck` event and the drive controller calls it where it restarts a Telling after `arrived`.

The two settings are `subtitle_size` ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium") and `subtitle_background` (bool, default true), declared where Game calls Settings.setup and applied the moment Settings emits `changed`. All sizes, margins, colours and the four numbers of 16.6 are in data/tuning.json (group subtitles_view, 17 constants with units). `--say=<line id>[,...]` requests lines at the start of the drive scene through the bus. Edits to shared files are small: 7 lines in drive_controller.gd, 2 hunks in game.gd, 4 lines in drive.tscn. I also added one `--say` run to the existing tools/smoke_all.gd so the path is under check.sh. Nothing under src/core, tests/ or docs/ was touched.

Merging: with the simulation branch (71dcfee) it merges with no conflict. With m10/postfx there is one conflict, in scenes/drive.tscn, because both add a CanvasLayer at the same place; keep both blocks, PostFX first, then Subtitles (tuning.json and drive_controller.gd auto-merge).

decisions: The view is src/view/subtitles_view.gd (SubtitlesView), not the subtitle_view.gd of GDD 13.2, and its wrapping, timing and queue are the pure class SubtitleQueue in src/view/subtitle_queue.gd.

A character is one code point of the text as the line table holds it (spaces counted, the speaker tag not); a text is cut only at spaces, tabs and line ends, and a single word longer than 42 characters is cut where the line ends.
Two lines are balanced: the same words are cut where the two lines differ least in length, the upper line the shorter on a tie; greedy filling decides only which words share a part.

A text that needs more than two lines is shown in parts of two lines, one after the other, each held for max(1.5 s, 0.06 s x its own characters), so a long text is held somewhat longer than the rule applied to the whole.

A subtitle's time begins with the frame it is first drawn in and it is taken away on the first frame at which its whole duration has passed (never less, up to a frame more); the clock is the view's own frame time, so it stops while the tree is paused, and there is no fade or gap between subtitles.
Lines asked for while one is showing wait in an unbounded first-in first-out queue; nothing is dropped or interrupted except by a clear.

A row that holds an exchange (speaker column 'X, then Y', text 'a / b', as GDD 3.6 writes the wreck lines and the proverb) is shown as one subtitle per speaker in order, each under their own name and timed by its own length; a row whose text does not hold as many parts as it names speakers is shown whole under the speaker column as written.

Speaker names are lines of their own, `speaker.` plus the name in lower case with underscores ('Old woman' is speaker.old_woman), resolved by Lines.get_speaker_name from what the speaker column holds; nine were added to both line files, and a speaker with no such line (or a name written in Arabic) is shown as the column has it.

The speaker tag is a row of its own above the text (0.8 of the text's size, orange #F5A742), not an inline prefix, so it does not count toward the 42 characters and each label keeps its own automatic text direction.

A `wreck` on the Events bus clears what is showing and waiting (the Wreck cuts off what was being said, GDD 3.2), so the Table's objection must be requested after the `wreck` event; the drive controller also calls clear() where it begins a Telling again after `arrived`.
The Subtitles layer stands after PostFX and before the Overlay in drive.tscn, so subtitles are drawn over the post effects and under the pointer (the tree of GDD 13.5 has no pointer layer).

Settings keys: `subtitle_size` is one of the names in tuning's subtitle_font_sizes ('small', 'medium', 'large' = 28, 36, 48 px at 1080p; default 'medium') and `subtitle_background` is a boolean (default true); a size name tuning does not have is shown as medium with a warning.

With the background off the letters keep their black outline (0.14 of their size) and nothing moves; with it on they stand on a #101014 box at 60% opacity with rounded corners, 48 px above the bottom edge.

`--say=<line id>[,<line id>...]` (not in GDD 13.9) requests those lines through the Events bus when the drive scene starts; an id the line table does not have is an engine error, so a misspelt id fails the smoke test.
The test line `subtitle.test.long` (143 characters, needs_writer false) was added to both line files because no line of GDD 3.6 is longer than two lines of 42 characters.

tools/subtitles_check.gd is a launcher and tools/subtitles_check_body.gd holds the checks, because a script started with --script is compiled before the autoload names exist; it is not a step of tools/check.sh, but tools/smoke_all.gd gained one drive run started with --say.
Right-to-left was verified with an Arabic line table built in memory (tools/subtitles_check.gd -- --rtl-shot=<png>), so lines_ar.csv stays empty as GDD 17.3 asks.
left_undone: GDD 17.3's font slot per language in settings is not built: the labels take the theme's font (Arabic was drawn here through the engine's system-font fallback), nothing calls Lines.set_locale, and GDD 17.1 has no language setting.
